Prior settings for fp_occu()

Source: R/fp_occu.R
fp_priors.Rd

Normal priors on the logit scale. The defaults are weakly informative for standardized covariates.

Usage

fp_priors(
  intercept_sd = 1.5,
  slope_sd = 2.5,
  gap_mean = 2,
  gap_sd = 1.5,
  recorder_sd = 2,
  fp_site_sd = 1
)

Arguments

intercept_sd

Standard deviation of the Normal(0, sd) priors on the intercepts of occupancy, true detection, and verified detection.

slope_sd

Standard deviation of the Normal(0, sd) priors on all slopes, including those of the false-positive rate.

gap_mean, gap_sd

Mean and standard deviation of the Normal prior, truncated at zero, on the gap between the true-detection and false-positive intercepts. The default, Normal(2, 1.5), puts the false-positive rate at the reference roughly an order of magnitude below true detection, while leaving room for the data.

recorder_sd

Scale of the half-Normal(0, sd) prior on the standard deviation of the recorder random intercept.

fp_site_sd

Scale of the half-Normal(0, sd) prior on the standard deviation of the site random intercept on the false-positive rate (fp_occu(random_fp = TRUE)).

Value

A list of class fp_priors.

Examples

fp_priors()
#> <fp_priors> (logit scale)
#>   intercepts      ~ Normal(0, 1.5)
#>   slopes          ~ Normal(0, 2.5)
#>   fp_gap          ~ Normal(2, 1.5), truncated at 0
#>   sd_recorder     ~ half-Normal(0, 2)
#>   sd_fp_site      ~ half-Normal(0, 1)
fp_priors(slope_sd = 1)
#> <fp_priors> (logit scale)
#>   intercepts      ~ Normal(0, 1.5)
#>   slopes          ~ Normal(0, 1)
#>   fp_gap          ~ Normal(2, 1.5), truncated at 0
#>   sd_recorder     ~ half-Normal(0, 2)
#>   sd_fp_site      ~ half-Normal(0, 1)
